title: Field-based Sky Replacement and Distort+Scale Wide-Angle Lookup in Baffin Island Landscape

locations.name: Baffin Island, Canada
locations.basis: explicit mention in transcript: 'considering we're in Baffin Island' and observed jet trail over a lake

summary: The video presents a field-driven landscape post-processing workflow centered on sky replacement and perspective correction to achieve a wide-angle look. The host describes planning and visualizing the final composite in the field, selecting a background sky and foreground elements, rotating and flipping the sky to match side lighting, and blending with controlled opacity and saturation. Foreground cleanup uses a 90% hard-edge brush to refine rocks and preserve a usable original element as a fallback. The tutorial covers a three-blend sky insertion, then applies Distort + Scale for a trapezoidal warp that emulates wide-angle distortion, guided by the horizon and 'rule of trapezoids' rather than conventional two-by-three crops. Water depth is enhanced with mid-tone dodging, and final decisions keep the sky blue with minimal dodging or vignette unless warranted. The speaker also emphasizes the importance of visualizing the composition in the field and notes timing and light-direction considerations unique to the Baffin Island environment.

sections.title: Field planning and perspective blending
concepts: discussion of perspective blending in the field
sections.description: The presenter notes the workflow goal and begins setting up the composite, mentioning the need to blend perspective in the field and selecting a background with significant foreground action to carry the shot.

sections.title: Foreground cleanup and rock adjustment
concepts: reintegrating the original rock if needed
sections.description: Fore- ground cleanup is described, including sharpening rock edges and the option to reintroduce the original rock if the cleanup removes too much detail, using a hard-edge brush with high certainty.

sections.title: Sky replacement workflow and lighting match
concepts: rotate and horizontal flip for side-light consistency
sections.description: Sky is selected and inserted into the scene, rotated/flip-paired to match afternoon side-light. The sky is painted in with measured opacity, saturation tweaks, and subtle blending to merge with the background.

sections.title: Distort + Scale and trapezoidal warp for a wide-angle look
sections.description: The method emphasizes Distort + Scale as a way to simulate wide-angle distortion. The speaker discusses using a trapezoidal warp to mimic lens distortion, notes the horizon should be centered, and rejects 2x3 crops in favor of 4x5 formats for the composition.

sections.title: Spot cleanup and jet-trail removal
sections.description: Small blemishes and an unexpected jet trail are removed from the frame, illustrating in-field cleanup steps that refine the final composite.

sections.title: Mid-tone dodging to enhance water depth
sections.description: Mid-tone dodging is used to brighten the lake’s mid-tones, which adds depth to the water without altering its color.

sections.title: Final color stance and light considerations
concepts: recognize diminishing light and its impact on the shot
sections.description: The sky remains blue to avoid a dramatic color shift; the speaker notes that additional effects like a vignette or minor dodging could be added, but stresses restraint due to changing light conditions.

sections.title: Sun star shot and conclusion
sections.description: A brief nod to a sun-star treatment is mentioned as a potential finish, followed by a short closing remark.

featured_techniques.technique: Sky replacement with lighting matching via rotation/flip
Rule of trapezoids and cropping decisions (4x5 preferred)
Mid-tone dodging to enhance water depth
